description: Somos un equipo conformado por 5 integrantes que estamos interesado en crear una solución a una problemática de la NASA, tenemos habilidades de codificación, estadísticas, desarrollo de software, ingles, interpretación y redacción.
summary:
Mission Architect is an interactive space mission engineering simulator and strategy web game built for NASA Space Apps 2026. Players step into the role of a mission commander to design, balance, launch, and operate robotic spacecraft missions to Low Earth Orbit (1.0 AU), Mars (1.52 AU), and Jupiter (5.2 AU).

Our project addresses the challenge of making complex aerospace systems engineering and mission trade-off analysis accessible, visual, and engaging. Inside a Master Equipment List (MEL) Hangar, players must balance launch vehicle mass limits, +25% dry-mass margins, the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation (Δv), inverse-square solar power attenuation (1/r²), Deep Space Network (DSN) downlink bandwidth, and Discovery/New Frontiers budget caps. Players then pilot their spacecraft in a live 2D orbital simulation—surviving solar storms, eclipses, and DSN congestion—while competing on a real-time PHP/MySQL leaderboard to maximize scientific return at the lowest cost.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Mission Architect is a four-stage space mission design and simulation web application:

1. Mission Briefing: Commanders select a team name, destination (LEO at 1.0 AU with a $150M cap, Mars at 1.52 AU with a $500M Discovery cap, or Jupiter at 5.2 AU with a $1,000M New Frontiers cap), primary science objective, and orbital trajectory (Direct Transfer vs. Gravity Assist).

2. MEL Hangar (Master Equipment List): Players assemble their spacecraft by choosing a launch vehicle (VADR, Medium, or Heavy), propulsion (Chemical Bipropellant or Solar Electric Ion), propellant mass, power system (solar arrays or Plutonium-238 MMRTGs), DSN communications (S, X, or Ka-band), bus/ADCS shielding, and 1–4 scientific instruments (+45% science bonus when aligned with the mission objective). A dynamic HTML5 Canvas renders the spacecraft in real time alongside five live engineering telemetry bars.

3. 2D Active Flight Simulation: A Canvas-based orbital simulator animates the flight across four mission phases (Launch, Cruise, Science Capture, and DSN Downlink) with speed controls (1x/2x/4x/Pause) and synthesized Web Audio sound effects. Players must make real-time engineering decisions during three flight anomalies: a Solar Storm (integrating NASA DONKI flare alerts with offline fallback), a Planetary Eclipse, and DSN Antenna Congestion.

4. Mission Report & Global Leaderboard: Outputs mission status, Cost-per-Science efficiency KPIs, engineering diagnostics, and a comparison with real NASA missions (PACE, MRO/MAVEN, Juno/Europa Clipper), saving every run to a live MySQL leaderboard.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Mission Architect helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts intuitively understand why spacecraft engineering is a constant trade-off between mass, power, delta-v, communications bandwidth, and budget—turning real NASA mission constraints into an engaging, replayable learning tool.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas (2D spacecraft preview and orbital simulation), Web Audio API (synthesized audio effects).

- Backend & Database: PHP (PDO REST API) and MySQL (missions_log leaderboard).

- External Data: NASA DONKI API and NASA/JPL mission reference parameters.

Creativity & Engineering Factors Considered:

Instead of static spreadsheets, we combined procedural 2D graphics and synthesized audio with real physics and NASA guidelines: Tsiolkovsky's rocket equation for Δv, inverse-square solar irradiance drop-off (P = P_1AU / r²), a +25% preliminary dry-mass margin, DSN frequency/weather trade-offs, and transparent separation between real NASA data, live physics calculations, and game assumptions.

AI / Super Intelligence (SI) Transparency Note:

AI assistance was used to support code debugging, UI/UX refinement, cloud deployment troubleshooting, and English documentation drafting. All engineering logic, NASA physics formulas, and final testing were reviewed and validated by our team.
